definitions.explanation: A feeling or impression, especially an unpleasant or unsettling one. Often used in the compound {気味|きみ}が{悪|わる}い (creepy, unsettling).
Used as a suffix (～{気味|ぎみ}) after nouns or verb stems to indicate a slight tendency or early signs of a condition, often something undesirable.

examples.japanese: {気味|きみ}が{悪|わる}い{話|はなし}だ。
{誰|だれ}もいないはずの{部屋|へや}から{物音|ものおと}がして、{気味|きみ}が{悪|わる}かった。
examples.english: I heard sounds from a room that should have been empty, and it was unsettling.

examples.japanese: あの{笑|わら}い{方|かた}はどこか{気味|きみ}が{悪|わる}い。
examples.english: There's something creepy about that laugh.
I have a touch of a cold.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}{太|ふと}り{気味|ぎみ}なので、{運動|うんどう}を{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: I've been putting on a bit of weight lately, so I started exercising.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}が{遅|おく}れ{気味|ぎみ}で、{残業|ざんぎょう}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: Work has been running a bit behind schedule, so I've been doing overtime.

notes:
GRAMMAR:
As a standalone noun, {気味|きみ} is most commonly used in the phrase {気味|きみ}が{悪|わる}い (creepy, unsettling). As a suffix, it attaches to nouns or verb stems with the reading ぎみ (voiced): {風邪|かぜ}{気味|ぎみ}, {太|ふと}り{気味|ぎみ}, {遅|おく}れ{気味|ぎみ}.

Note the reading difference: {気味|きみ} as a standalone word vs. ～{気味|ぎみ} as a suffix.

Do not confuse with the homophone {君|きみ} (you), which uses different kanji.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {気味|きみ}が{悪|わる}い: creepy, unsettling
- {風邪|かぜ}{気味|ぎみ}: touch of a cold
- {太|ふと}り{気味|ぎみ}: slightly overweight
- {遅|おく}れ{気味|ぎみ}: running a bit behind
- {疲|つか}れ{気味|ぎみ}: somewhat tired
